# Install necessary packages if you don't have them
install.packages(c("lme4", "sjPlot", "lmerTest", "broom.mixed"))

library(lme4)      # For the mixed model
library(lmerTest)  # Provides p-values for lme4 models
library(sjPlot)    # For the beautiful publication table
library(broom.mixed) # For tidying model outputs

# 1. Load the data
df <- read.csv("combined_cohort_disease_results.csv")

# 2. Fit the Linear Mixed Effects Model
# We use lmer from lmerTest to get Satterthwaite's degrees of freedom (p-values)
model <- lmer(balanced_accuracy_disease ~ balanced_accuracy_cohort + (1|model) + (1|train) + (1|test), 
              data = df)

# 3. View a detailed summary in the console
summary(model)

# 4. Generate a Publication-Ready Table
# This creates an HTML table you can open in a browser or paste into Word
tab_model(model, 
          show.re.var = TRUE,          # Show Random Effect Variances
          show.icc = TRUE,             # Show Intraclass Correlation
          p.style = "numeric_stars",   # Use stars for p-values (* < 0.05, etc)
          title = "Table 1: Linear Mixed Model of Disease BACC vs. Cohort BACC",
          dv.labels = "Disease BACC (Dependent Variable)",
          string.pred = "Predictors",
          digits = 4,
          digits.re = 6,
          file = "local/output/model_table.html")    # Saves the table to a file

library(broom.mixed)

# 1. Get the Fixed Effects (Estimate, Std.Error, p-value)
fixed_df <- tidy(model, effects = "fixed")
print("--- Fixed Effects ---")
print(fixed_df)

# 2. Get the Random Effects (Variances and Standard Deviations)
random_df <- tidy(model, effects = "ran_pars")
print("--- Random Effects ---")
print(random_df)
